layout_dets.text: FIVES: A Fundus Image Dataset for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Artificial Intelligence based Vessel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Kai JinD1,5, Xingru Huang²,5, Jingxing Zhou1,5, Yunxiang Li³, Yan Yan1, Yibao Sun²,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Qianni Zhang², Yaqi Wang4,6& Juan Ye1,6

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Retinal vasculature provides an opportunity for direct observation of vessel morphology, which is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: linked to multiple clinical conditions. However, objective and quantitative interpretation of the retinal

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vasculature relies on precise vessel segmentation, which is time consuming and labor intensive.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Artificial intelligence (Al) has demonstrated great promise in retinal vessel segmentation. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: development and evaluation of Al-based models require large numbers of annotated retinal images.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: However, the public datasets that are usable for this task are scarce. In this paper, we collected a color

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fundus image vessel segmentation (FIVES) dataset. The FIVES dataset consists of 800 high-resolution

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: multi-disease color fundus photographs with pixelwise manual annotation. The annotation process

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: was standardized through crowdsourcing among medical experts. The quality of each image was also

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: evaluated. To the best of our knowledge, this is the largest retinal vessel segmentation dataset for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which we believe this work will be beneficial to the further development of retinal vessel segmentation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Background & Summary

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Retinal vasculature is a reliable reflection of vessel morphologic changes, which have been demonstrated to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: relate to numerous clinical conditions, including both ophthalmological and systemic diseases. Diabetic retin-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: opathy (DR), age-related macular degeneration (AMD), and glaucoma are major blindness-causing diseases¹.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Multiple studies have investigated the relationship between retinal vasculature characteristics and these ocular

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: diseases2-4. Some life-threatening systemic diseases can also be reflected in fundus images, such as cardiovas-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cular diseases⁵ and neurological disorders6. Several retinal vessel morphometrics are thought to be linked to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: disease risk and progression7-10. Retinal vessel segmentation, which means the extraction of visible vasculature

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from a fundus image (Fig. 1a), is the preliminary step to objectively assessing the fundus image vasculature and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: quantitatively interpreting the morphometrics.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Retinal vessel segmentation is a challenging task, considering that age, ophthalmic disease, and photograph

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: conditions all have a considerable impact on segmentation. In children, there is a prominent sheen from the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: retinal nerve fibers near the vessels and macula, blocking the view of the connections between vessels (Fig. 1b).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In elderly adults, hypoplasia of the retinal pigment epithelium leaves the choroidal vessels visible, similar to the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: retinal vasculature (Fig. 1c). Microaneurysms, hemorrhages, and exudates can be seen on fundus images of dia-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: betic retinopathy patients (Fig. 1d). Eye movements and improper operations can result in loss of focus (Fig. 1e)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and insufficient exposure (Fig. 1f).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In retinal image analysis, manual segmentation of retinal blood vessels is extremely time consuming and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: labour intensive, unlike other retinal image preprocessing tasks such as artery-vein classification, which is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: important but can be done manually while conducting medical studies. Automated and semiautomated vessel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation is thus an indispensable process for efficient quantitative interpretation of the retinal vasculature.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Many studies have been conducted on retinal vessel segmentation, including conventional algorithms¹ and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Table 1. Summarization of publicly available retinal vessel segmentation datasets.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: artificial intelligence (AI) based segmentation12. AI based methods have been intensively studied in recent years.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The development and evaluation of AI-based methods requires datasets with large amounts of annotated images.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Several retinal vessel segmentation datasets, which are summarized in Table 1, have been established for public

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: use: STARE13, DRIVE14, ARIA15, REVIEW16, CHASEDB117, HRF18, etc. Nearly all retinal vessel segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: work has been carried out on these datasets, including state-of-the-art vessel segmentation algorithms, such as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SCS-Net19, the NFN + model20 and the MS-DRIS-GP model21. There are also algorithms that can do a simultane-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ous segmentation and artery-vein classification developed on these datasets, such as the work of Hemelings et al.22.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: However, there are some inherent drawbacks of these popular datasets:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: •First, the images included in these datasets are small in quantity and imbalanced in disease distribution, and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: most of them are of low resolution. A small quantity may lead to overfitting when using deep learning. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: distribution of disease is rather imbalanced, for which disease-specific analysis cannot be conducted. Some of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the most commonly used datasets have resolutions of less than 1000 × 1000 pixels23.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Second, the annotation process has not been standardized by healthcare professionals, so inappropriate anno-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tations may occur. For example, some pathological changes will form a strip-like structure and should not be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: labelled as retinal vessels, as is shown in Fig. 2.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: •Third, image quality, which is an important factor affecting the segmentation performance, is not evaluated.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Providing the evaluation of images will be useful for further in-depth research into the question of how the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: performance of methods is affected by image quality.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Taking all of these factors into consideration, it would be meaningful to establish a public retinal vessel seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentation dataset with pixelwise annotation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In this paper, we propose a fundus image vessel segmentation (FIVES) dataset consisting of 800

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: high-resolution color fundus photographs with pixelwise manual annotation through standard crowdsourcing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: among medical staff. For each image, 3 labels were provided: disease, pixelwise vessel annotation and image

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: quality scores. Our major contributions can be summarized as follows:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Image: The dataset contains 800 high-resolution images of normal eyes and 3 different eye diseases, with 200

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: images in each category.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Annotation: Pixelwise annotation was performed by a group of trained medical staff and verified by experi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: enced ophthalmologists who had been annotating for hundreds of hours. The annotation group was made up

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation research and promote translation from technology to clinical use.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Methods

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Data collection. Eight hundred color fundus photographs were collected from 2016 to 2021 in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Ophthalmology Centre at the Second Affiliated Hospital of Zhejiang University (SHAZU) (Fig. 3a). These

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: images are from 573 patients, with ages ranging from 4 to 83 years. Written informed consent complying with the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: requirement of the Medical Ethics Committee of SHAZU was signed by every participant when it was decided

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that their photographs would be adopted by scientific research. The study followed the tenets of the Helsinki

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Declaration and was approved by the Medical Ethics Committee of SAHZU. The study has been registered on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ClinicalTrials.gov with trial registration number NCT04718532.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Patients underwent comprehensive systemic and ocular examinations to establish a diagnosis. Before pho-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tographing, 2 to 3 drops of 1.0% tropicamide phenylephrine were used for pupil dilation of every examined eye.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Pupils with diameters over 7 millimeters were considered fully dilated, and fundus photographs were taken. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: images were captured by tabletop TRC-NW8 fundus cameras at a 50° field of view (Topcon Medical Systems,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Tokyo, Japan) and centered at the macula. For a 50° field of view, both the macula and the optic disc could be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: seen in the image. The photographing process was conducted by experienced examiners. For each examined eye,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: only one photograph was included in the final dataset. For each patient, both eyes were examined. All the images

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: were collected and manually selected to form the final dataset. The manual selection considered both disease

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: diagnosis and image readability. Selection criteria considering disease diagnosis can be found below, and we

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: have intentionally included about 5% images with poor readability assessed by experienced ophthalmic doctors

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to reflect real clinical situation. Pictures were saved in PNG format with a resolution of 2048 × 2048 pixels. No

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image compression was conducted during the image capturing, annotation and dataset uploading processes.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Disease diagnosis. In this study, only patients with a clearly ascertained diagnosis were included. The diag-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nostic procedure started with first-contact doctors and was further reviewed by experienced ophthalmologic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: specialists. The diagnosis criteria complied with most updated American Academy of Ophthalmology's guidelines

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: at the time when the picture was taken. Details are described below:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: For DR, both type 1 and type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM) patients were considered. The diagnosis of DM was

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: based on the criteria proposed by the American Diabetes Association²4. Examinations necessary for the diagno-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sis of DM were conducted before image capture, including slit-lamp examination, ultrawide fundus photogra-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: phy, optical coherence tomography and fundus florescence angiography, when necessary. Images with laser scars

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: were also included to mimic real clinical practice.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Patients with age-related macular degeneration (AMD) underwent thorough ocular examinations, including

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: slit-lamp examination, fundus photography, optical coherence tomography (OCT) and fundus fluorescein angi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ography, if necessary. Pathological features in fundus images include drusen, exudate, geographic atrophy or hem-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: orrhage. The diagnostic procedure was conducted according to the AAO's Preferred Practice Pattern for AMD25.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: For glaucoma, both open-angle glaucoma and angle-closure glaucoma were included in this study. Patients of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: this kind often present headache, decreased vision, elevated intraocular pressure (IOP) and optic nerve damage,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which can be seen in fundus photographs. The diagnosis of glaucoma is based on clinical complaints, IOP, fun-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dus photography, visual field examination and optical coherence tomography. The detailed diagnostic criteria

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: can be found in AAO's Preferred Practice Pattern of glaucoma26,27.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The exclusion criteria included patients with an uncertain diagnosis, patients with multiple diseases, patients

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with excessive opacity in refractive media, patients with systemic diseases other than DM that can affect the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: retina, patients with familial ocular diseases, and patients with ocular trauma.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Vessel annotation. The annotation process started with the recruitment of annotators (Fig. 3b). The recruit-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ment message was posted online and shared via social media, requesting that medical workers who were willing to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: www.nature.com/scientificdata/

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Fig. 3 Workflow of the establishment of the proposed dataset. (a) Eight hundred color fundus photographs

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: were collected in the Ophthalmology Center at the Second Affiliated Hospital of Zhejiang University (SHAZU).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: These photographs comprised 200 images from patients diagnosed with diabetic retinopathy (DR), 200 from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: patients with glaucoma, 200 from patients with age-related macular degeneration (AMD), and 200 from normal

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: controls. (b) The annotation team was made up of 3 senior annotators and 24 junior annotators who had

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: completed guideline-based training and image annotation tests. (c) The interface of the specifically designed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: annotating software used in this study. (d) The annotation process consisted of initial annotation by junior

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: annotators and further verification by senior annotators. Each image was randomly assigned to 2 annotators,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and the common pixels annotated by both of them were included as the result of initial annotation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: participate and well aware of the retina anatomy could join in this work. Finally, the annotation group consisted of 3

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ophthalmic practitioners with clinical ophthalmic experience and 24 medical staff meeting the recruitment criteria.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The training of annotators was an important part of the annotation process (Fig.3b). A detailed annotation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: guideline was made by 3 ophthalmic practitioners of SAHZU. For each annotator, having learned the annotation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: guidelines, 5 test images, including 1 normal, 2 DR, 1glaucoma and 1 AMD, were assigned and retrieved after

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: their initial annotation. The test images were evaluated by the ophthalmic practitioner one by one. If the anno-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tation result was not satisfiable, the image was sent back to the student for relabeling. If the results of relabeling

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: were still unacceptable, the annotators could not enter the next stage of annotation work. If the test images were

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: thought to be appropriately labeled, more images would be assigned. Annotators were paid differently according

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to their annotation performance, which was qualitatively evaluated by senior annotators and project managers

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: based on three aspects: false positive pixels, false negative pixels and overall vasculature.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The annotation was achieved using specifically designed annotating software. Figure 3c shows the annotating

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: interface. Annotators were asked to use the pencil tool to color the pixel white if they thought it was a vessel pixel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: based on the appearance. In some images, the vessels seemed broken due to various reasons. To ensure that the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: annotated pixels were from vessels and reduce false positive annotation, annotators were told that no modifi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cation should be made just to maintain the continuity of the vasculature. The final vessel segmentation ground

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: www.nature.com/scientificdata/

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Fig. 4 Image quality assessment and data split. (a) Illustration of image quality evaluation process. (b) Data split

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: strategy.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: truth is a two-color image, with white pixels meaning vessel and black for non-vessel pixels. The resolution of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ground truth is 2048 × 2048 pixels, coordinated with the original fundus image.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In the official annotation stage (Fig.3d), each annotator was assigned over 30 images. Each image was anno-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tated by 2 annotators. The pixels annotated by the 2 annotators in common were included as the final ground

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: truth of the specific image to reduce the number of false positive pixels. Annotating one image would take

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: approximately 3–5 hours. The overall annotation process began in December 2020 and ended in June 2021.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: After being annotated by junior annotators, the images were further reviewed by senior annotators to correct

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: errors, such as misidentification of the choroidal vessels as retinal vessels. If there were clear mistakes, the senior

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: annotators would directly correct them when reviewing. If the senior annotators disagreed with the annotation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: results but were not certain, they would discuss the matter amongst themselves and then make the final decision.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Image quality assessment. Considering that the color fundus image quality was substantially influenced

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by various factors and to make the dataset usable for different research purposes, each image of the FIVES dataset

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: was evaluated on three image quality aspects: illumination and color distortion, blur, and low contrast distortion.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The assessment procedure was realized by previously published automatic algorithms28. For each aspect, a score,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: either 0 or 1, was given to represent the quality (Fig. 4a). The image quality gradation grants researchers the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: opportunity to investigate the robustness of the proposed algorithm.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In AI-based image processing, there should be at least 2 subsets, which are the training set used for learning and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the test set used for testing. There should be no intersection between the 2 sets. To fully test an algorithm's capac-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ity, the characteristics should be distributed equally between these sets. Therefore, we recommend the data split

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: strategy based on the aforementioned image quality score. This process was realized by manual selection (Fig. 4b).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Data Records

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The FIVES dataset has been uploaded to Figshare in the form of a zipped file29. The unzipped file folder contains

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the original fundus photographs, annotation ground truth images and quality assessment scores. The unzipped

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: file is organized into 2 folders and 1 Microsoft office Excel list, named "train", "test" and “Quality Assessment.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: xlsx", respectively. The folders contain the images that are recommended for training and testing. The images in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: these 2 folders are stored, named and arranged in the same way. In the “train" folder, there are 2 subfolders named

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: "Original" and “Ground Truth" that contain original fundus images and corresponding ground truth images,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: respectively. Images are named "n_A/D/G/N.png", where "n" means the number of images and "A", "D", "G”, and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: "N” stand for "AMD", "DR", "Glaucoma" and "Normal”, respectively. In the "Ground Truth" folder, images are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: named according to the same rule, where a specific image in this folder is the ground truth of the image with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the same name in the “Original". "n" is 600 in the training set and 200 in the test set. It should be noted that the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: current data split strategy is recommended by our team and can be altered for different research purposes. In the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: file “Quality Assessment.xlsx", there are 2 sheets titled “Train" and “Test", with 5 columns in each sheet. The first

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: column represents the disease diagnosis. The second column contains the number of specific images. The sub-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sequent columns represent the illumination and color distortion, blur, and low contrast scores. The image assess-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ment score is either 1 or 0, with 1 indicating good quality in this specific aspect and 0 indicating poor quality.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: TechnicalValidation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Dataset characteristics. There are 800 fundus images and their corresponding ground truth images in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: FIVES dataset. These pictures are from 573 subjects. The mean age of the subjects was 48 years, with a standard

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: deviation of 19.87 years. There were 469 images from female subjects and 331 from males. All the subjects were

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Asian. The number and proportion of annotated vessel pixels are summarized in Table 2. The mean image quality

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: scores are summarized in Table 3. Most images were of high quality in terms of the 3 aspects. It is worth noting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that images from glaucoma patients tend to have fewer annotated pixels and lower illumination and color dis-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tortion scores. We suspect this is because most glaucoma patients are older and may have more opacity in their

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: refractive media, causing insufficient illumination, which would then influence the annotation ratio. The inclu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sion of some low-quality images can help reflect clinical reality and test the algorithms' robustness.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Intra- and inter-annotator consistency. There are some automatic retinal vessel segmentation algo-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rithms that can be used to segment vessels automatically. However, to the best of our knowledge, the best perfor-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mance of the proposed algorithms yielded a Dice coefficient of approximately 0.82, the Dice coefficient being a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: value that reflects the accuracy of segmentation¹9. For this specific task, the accuracy is not satisfiable enough to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: generate a reliable dataset, which is why we opted for manual annotation. In this work, every image was annotated

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by 2 junior annotators and refined by 1 senior annotator. Therefore, three kinds of consistencies should be inves-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tigated: intra-annotator consistency of the same annotator at different times, inter-annotator consistency of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: same-level annotators and inter-annotator consistency of different-level annotators. Corresponding experiments

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: were conducted to investigate these kinds of error.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: For intra-annotator consistency of the same annotator at different times, 40 images of the whole dataset were

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: selected and extracted to form an example set based on the disease diagnosis and image quality. The example set

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: consisted of 10 images of each diagnosis category and 5–8 low-quality images of each image quality assessment

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: aspect. Five annotators from the annotation group, 1 senior and 4 junior annotators, were asked to annotate

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the 40 images 2 times in one month, with at least a 1-week gap between each annotation. The Dice coefficient

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: was calculated between the 1st and 2nd annotations. Mean Dice was computed for all 40 images and 4 anno-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tators. The mean Dice was 0.9679 (0.9602–0.9810), which means the annotators' labeling was stable and the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: intra-annotator error was small.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: For inter-annotator consistency of the same-level annotators, the error was evaluated using Dice between

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: annotations generated by 2 annotators. The original annotation results without refinement were used to investi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: gate this error. The mean Dice was 0.9241 (0.8792–0.9823), which means that the annotation results were close

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: between junior annotators.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: For inter-annotator consistency of different-level annotators, the 1st annotations were used for the analysis in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: this question. The Dice coefficient was calculated between 1 senior annotator's vessel mask and 4 junior annota-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tors' annotations. Mean dice was computed. The mean Dice of the annotators was 0.9608 (0.9564–0.9676), which

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: means that the disagreement among annotators of different levels was small.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Through the analysis of original annotations and the example set, we can conclude that annotations were sta-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ble and consistent between one annotator at different times and different annotators, which lays the groundwork

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for accurate annotation and repeatable retinal vessel segmentation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Usage Notes

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The whole dataset can be downloaded from the link mentioned above. It is worth noting that the data split strat-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: egy was made considering the image quality and disease diagnosis. We recommend that users follow this strategy

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to make the dataset balanced. However, they can always split the strategy according to their study design. For

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: researchers who use traditional algorithms rather than artificial intelligence, the data split is not applicable. Users

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: should cite this paper in their research output and acknowledge the contribution of this dataset in their study.
